summary: Deterministic cross-level audit of all six A1-C2 blueprints (a1-c2), resolving the placeholder cross-level prerequisite reconciliations that B1, C1 and C2's own blueprints explicitly asked this task to perform once the real predecessor blueprints existed. Built the full capability id graph (including Pre-A1 required core), normalized six differing per-level JSON schemas, and found: 3 cross-level capability-id collisions with incompatible or duplicated semantics (report_a_problem a2/b1, infer_implied_meaning b2/c1, reformulate_for_a_different_audience c1/c2 -- the last directly contradicting C2's own 'first mediation task' claim); 19 broken/unresolved cross-level prerequisite strings across B1 (6), C1 (6) and C2 (7), each mapped to a concrete real-id replacement at high or medium confidence except one flagged low-confidence row needing human judgment; a full-level CEFR-reference gap in A2 (0/19 capabilities, the only level missing this template-required field); duplicate CORE-engine requirement asks from B2 and C1 for the same register-appropriateness and discourse-coherence evaluator capabilities; a semantic-type fragmentation risk across B1's problem/B2's problem_type/C1's proposed negotiated_item, directly answering C1's own explicit request to check this before building twice; and two pattern-id reuse risks (because_reason_pattern a2/b1, hedging_pattern b2/c2) with genuine false-mastery/spacing implications for the shared retrieval-practice engine, not just naming hygiene. Zero prerequisite cycles found in any level. Confirmed B2's cross-level references (authored after B1 landed) all resolve cleanly -- the target pattern the other four boundaries should match. All six blueprints correctly stay available:false and reaffirm A1's fail-closed state. This task's write scope (docs/curriculum/cross-level-audit.{md,json} only) does not include the blueprint files that need these fixes; every fix is handed to LC-FND-002 (whose write scope covers docs/curriculum/**) via .ai/foundry/requests/LC-AUD-001.md, per the coordination contract's rule against quietly implementing out-of-scope changes. No blueprint edited, no runtime code touched, no level opened. This audit proves design-artifact cross-level consistency only; it does not certify pedagogical approval or real-learner efficacy.
